arxiv-1609-07774.title: Demonstrating non-Abelian braiding of surface code defects in a five qubit experiment
arxiv-1609-07774.creator: James R. Wootton
arxiv-1609-07774.description: Abstract Currently, the mainstream approach to quantum computing is through surface codes. One way to store and manipulate quantum information with these to create defects in the codes which can be moved and used as if they were particles. Specifically, they simulate the behaviour of exotic particles known as Majoranas, which are a kind of non-Abelian anyon.

arxiv-2201-03119.title: Langlands functoriality conjecture for SO 2 ​ n ∗ \operatorname{\textbf{{SO}}}_{2n}^{*} in positive characteristic
arxiv-2201-03119.creator: Héctor del Castillo
arxiv-2201-03119.description: Abstract . In this article we are concerned with the Langlands functoriality conjecture. Cogdell, Kim, Piatetski-Shapiro and Shahidi proved functioriality conjecture in the case of a globally generic cuspidal automorphic representation for the split classical groups, unitary groups or even quasi-split special orthogonal groups in characteristic zero.

arxiv-2301-01718.title: An adaptive, training-free reduced-order model for convection-dominated problems based on hybrid snapshots Journal: Elsevier
arxiv-2301-01718.creator: Victor Zucatti, Matthew J. Zahr
arxiv-2301-01718.description: Abstract The vast majority of reduced-order models (ROMs) first obtain a low dimensional representation of the problem from high-dimensional model (HDM) training data which is afterwards used to obtain a system of reduced complexity. Unfortunately, convection-dominated problems generally have a slowly decaying Kolmogorov n n -width, which makes obtaining an accurate ROM built solely from training data very challenging.

arxiv-2311-17206.title: MUSE observations of the optical nebula surrounding the central compact object in the Vela Junior Supernova Remnant 2023 MUSE observations of the optical nebula surrounding the central compact object in the Vela Junior Supernova Remnant – References
arxiv-2311-17206.creator: Janette Suherli, Samar Safi-Harb, Ivo R. Seitenzahl, Parviz Ghavamian, Wynn C. G. Ho, Chuan-Jui Li, Ashley J. Ruiter, Ralph S. Sutherland, Frédéric P. A. Vogt
arxiv-2311-17206.description: Abstract Central Compact Objects (CCOs), neutron stars found near the centre of some Supernova Remnants (SNRs), have been almost exclusively studied in X-rays and are thought to lack the wind nebulae typically seen around young, rotation-powered pulsars. We present the first, spatially-resolved, morphological and spectroscopic study of the optical nebula observed at the location of CXOU J085201.

arxiv-2402-15131.title: Interactive-KBQA: Multi-Turn Interactions for Knowledge Base Question Answering with Large Language Models
arxiv-2402-15131.creator: Guanming Xiong, Junwei Bao, Wen Zhao
arxiv-2402-15131.description: Abstract This study explores the realm of knowledge base question answering (KBQA). KBQA is considered a challenging task, particularly in parsing intricate questions into executable logical forms. Traditional semantic parsing (SP)-based methods require extensive data annotations, which result in significant costs. Recently, the advent of few-shot in-context learning, powered by large language models (LLMs), has showcased promising capabilities.

arxiv-2404-04250.title: Dissipative Euler flows originating from circular vortex filaments
arxiv-2404-04250.creator: Francisco Gancedo, Antonio Hidalgo-Torné, Francisco Mengual
arxiv-2404-04250.description: Abstract In this paper, we prove the first existence result of weak solutions to the 3D Euler equation with initial vorticity concentrated in a circle and velocity field in C ⁡ ( [ 0 , T ] , L 2 − ) C([0,T],L^{2^{-}}) .

arxiv-2410-12874.title: On Debiasing Text Embeddings Through Context Injection
arxiv-2410-12874.creator: Thomas Uriot
arxiv-2410-12874.description: Abstract Current advances in Natural Language Processing (NLP) have made it increasingly feasible to build applications leveraging textual data. Generally, the core of these applications rely on having a good semantic representation of text into vectors, via embedding models. However, it has been shown that these embeddings capture and perpetuate biases already present in text.

arxiv-2412-04916.title: Dark Matter Annual Modulation Analysis with Combined Nuclear and Electron Recoil Channels
arxiv-2412-04916.creator: H.B. Li, M.K. Pandey, C.H. Leung, L. Singh, H.T. Wong, H.-C. Chi, M. Deniz, Greeshma C, J.-W. Chen, H.C. Hsu, S. Karadaǧ, S. Karmakar, V. Kumar, J. Li, F.K. Lin, S.T. Lin, C.-P. Liu, S.K. Liu, H. Ma, D.K. Mishra, K. Saraswat, V. Sharma, M.K. Singh, M.K. Singh, V. Singh, D. Tanabe, J.S. Wang, C.-P. W
arxiv-2412-04916.description: Abstract After decades of experimental efforts, the DAMA/LIBRA( DL \rm DL ) annual modulation (AM) analysis on the χ ​ N \chi{\rm N} (WIMP Dark Matter interactions on nucleus) channel remains the only one which can be interpreted as positive signatures. This has been refuted by numerous time-integrated (TI) and AM analysis.

arxiv-2503-01732.title: No Plan but Everything Under Control: Robustly Solving Sequential Tasks with Dynamically Composed Gradient Descent
arxiv-2503-01732.creator: Vito Mengers, Oliver Brock
arxiv-2503-01732.description: Abstract We introduce a novel gradient-based approach for solving sequential tasks by dynamically adjusting the underlying myopic potential field in response to feedback and the world’s regularities. This adjustment implicitly considers subgoals encoded in these regularities, enabling the solution of long sequential tasks, as demonstrated by solving the traditional planning domain of Blocks World— without any planning .

arxiv-2503-05695.title: Approximately Envy-free and Equitable Allocations of Indivisible Items for Non-monotone Valuations Thanks: This work was partially supported by: the Horizon EU Framework Programme under Grant agreement No 101183743 (AGATE); the PNRR MIUR project FAIR - Future AI Research (PE00000013), Spoke 9 - Gree
arxiv-2503-05695.creator: Vittorio Bilò, Martin Loebl, Cosimo Vinci
arxiv-2503-05695.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Vittorio Bilò, Martin Loebl, Cosimo Vinci. We revisit the setting of fair allocation of indivisible items among agents with heterogeneous, non-monotone valuations. We explore the existence and efficient computation of allocations that approximately satisfy either envy-freeness or equity constraints. Approximate envy-freeness ensures that each agent values her bundle at least as much as those given to the others, after some (or any) item removal, while approximate equity guarantees roughly equal valuations among agents, under similar adjustments.

arxiv-2506-11295.title: A Tale of Two Systems:Characterizing Architectural Complexity onMachine Learning-Enabled Systems
arxiv-2506-11295.creator: Renato Cordeiro Ferreira
arxiv-2506-11295.description: Abstract How can the complexity of ML-enabled systems be managed effectively? The goal of this research is to investigate how complexity affects ML-Enabled Systems (MLES). To address this question, this research aims to introduce a metrics-based architectural model to characterize the complexity of MLES.

arxiv-2508-05573.title: Bounds for spectral projectors on the three-dimensional torus
arxiv-2508-05573.creator: Pierre Germain 1, Simon L. Rydin Myerson 2, Daniel Pezzi 3
arxiv-2508-05573.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pierre Germain 1, Simon L. Rydin Myerson 2, Daniel Pezzi 3. We study L 2 L^{2} to L p L^{p} operator norms of spectral projectors for the Euclidean Laplacian on the torus in the case where the spectral window is narrow. With a window of constant size this is a classical result of Sogge; in the small-window limit we are left with L p L^{p} norms of eigenfunctions of the Laplacian, as considered for instance by Bourgain.

arxiv-2509-24238.title: Learning to Ponder: Adaptive Reasoning in Latent Space
arxiv-2509-24238.creator: Yixin HeUniversity of Southern California yixinhe@usc.edu, Lumingyuan TangIndependent Researcher tanglujay@gmail.com
arxiv-2509-24238.description: Abstract Test-time compute has emerged as a key paradigm for enhancing LLM reasoning, yet prevailing approaches like Best-of- N N and majority voting apply uniform depth across inputs, wasting computation on simple queries while potentially under-thinking complex ones. We present FR‑Ponder, a single‑graph, backbone‑training‑free framework that allocates instance‑adaptive reasoning compute via latent steering.

Cleri, Olivia R. Cooper, Karl Glazebrook, Rashmi Gottumukkala, Jenny E. Greene, Andy D. Goulding, Michaela Hirschmann, Ivo Labbe, Zach Lewis
arxiv-2510-25024.description: Abstract At low redshift, massive quiescent galaxies (MQGs) are most frequently found in massive, rich galaxy clusters, but at high redshift the trend is less clear. Here, we present spectroscopic evidence of the effects of environment on the formation and assembly of high-redshift MQGs. We identify 25 (5) log ⁡ ( M ∗ / M ⊙ ) ≥ 10.

arxiv-2601-01131.title: Notes on Poisson deformations of symplectic varieties
arxiv-2601-01131.description: Abstract §1. Introduction . We have proved some basic properties of the Poisson deformation of a symplectic variety (X,\omega) in [Na]. We call an affine symplectic variety (X,\omega) conical if X admits a good \mathbf{C}^{*} -action and \omega is homogeneous with weight l>0 .

pmc-10628816.title: Long non-coding RNA LHX1-DT regulates cardiomyocyte differentiation through H2A.Z-mediated LHX1 transcriptional activation
pmc-10628816.creator: Qi Yu, Benzhi Cai, Yong Zhang, Juan Xu, Dongping Liu, Xiyang Zhang, Zhenbo Han, Yingying Ma, Lei Jiao, Manyu Gong, Xuewen Yang, Yanying Wang, Haodong Li, Lihua Sun, Yu Bian, Fan Yang, Lina Xuan, Haodi Wu, Baofeng Yang, Ying Zhang
pmc-10628816.description: SummaryLong non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play widespread roles in various processes. However, there is still limited understanding of the precise mechanisms through which they regulate early stage cardiomyocyte differentiation. In this study, we identified a specific lncRNA called LHX1-DT, which is transcribed from a bidirectional promoter of LIM Homeobox 1 (LHX1) gene.

pmc-11550158.title: Method development and validation for the extraction and quantification of sesquiterpene lactones in Dolomiaea costus
pmc-11550158.creator: Mohammed Aldholmi
pmc-11550158.description: Graphical abstractKeywords: Costunolide, Dehydrocostus lactone, Qust, Kuth, Ultrasonic bath, Ultrasonic homogeniser Introduction Dolomiaea costus, formerly known as Saussurea costus and Aucklandia costus, is a medicinal plant belonging to the Asteraceae family [1]. It is native to the Himalayan regions of India, Pakistan, and China [2]. Dolomiaea costus is commonly known as Indian costus, Mu Xiang, costus, Kuth, or Qust [3].

pmc-11570299.title: A calibrated scale to measure heritage learning in digital environments. A network analysis approach
pmc-11570299.creator: Olaia Fontal, Alex Ibañez-Etxeberria, Víctor B. Arias, Benito Arias
pmc-11570299.description: To date, there have been scarcely any published studies dedicated to developing instruments with sufficient guarantees of accuracy, validity, and reliability for the assessment of heritage learning in digital contexts. Furthermore, very few such studies on this subject have employed the network analysis methodology.

pmc-11634108.title: Educational interventions improve disparities in patient access to kidney transplantation: a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-11634108.creator: Amanda Godoi, Georgios Koimtzis, Nicole Felix, Maria MR Mora, Augusto Graziani e Sousa, Giulia AR Soares, Pedro EP Carvalho, Mohamed A Ilham, Michael R Stephens, Usman Khalid
pmc-11634108.description: Background:Transplantation significantly improves the quality of life for patients with chronic kidney disease. Despite various educational strategies being assessed, the optimal approach to overcome barriers to kidney transplantation remains unclear.Materials and Methods:The authors conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing educational interventions to improve kidney transplantation access.

pmc-11641892.title: Clinical Insights into Sickle Cell Disease: A Comprehensive Multicenter Retrospective Analysis of Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes Across Different Age Groups
pmc-11641892.creator: Daniyah A. Almarghalani, Renad A. Alotaibi, Teef T. Alzlami, Ozouf F. Alhumaidi, Najla M. Alharthi, Fatimah M. Alboqami, Khulood A. Almehmadi, Samar F. pmc-11641892.description: Background: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a genetic hematological disorder associated with significant mortality and a range of complex complications that manifest differently across various age groups. Methods: This study aimed to evaluate the demographic, clinical, and laboratory characteristics of SCD patients in Taif City, Saudi Arabia, with a focus on variations among children, adolescents, adults, and middle-aged individuals.

pmc-12413744.title: Mapping advance care planning and advance directives in Latin America
pmc-12413744.creator: Natália Rocha Tardelli, Fernanda Bono Fukushima, Jenny T van der Steen, Manuel Iván Cobas Rodríguez, Rasa Mikelyte, Daniel Neves Forte, Alex Sander Watanabe Palácio, Vilma Adriana Tripodoro, Mirna Garcia Burgoa, Douglas Henrique Crispim, Alfredo Rodríguez-Núñez, Luis Ricardo González Cruz, Mariuska
pmc-12413744.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/aimsThe extent to which low- and middle-income countries have implemented Advance Care Planning (ACP) and Advance Directives (AD) remains unclear. We aimed to map the current status of ACP/AD in Latin America.MethodsThis cross-sectional, mixed-methods survey of ACP/AD in LA comprised interviews with 18 key informants from 18 out of 20 countries, most of whom were appointed by national Palliative Care Associations.

pmc-12675401.title: Developing scalable woven textile-based scaffolds for tubular tissues with Core–Sheath nanofibre yarns and tuneable weave architectures
pmc-12675401.creator: Anna Doersam, Luis Larrea Murillo, Celina Jones, Olga Tsigkou
pmc-12675401.description: IntroductionEngineering functional tubular tissues requires scaffolds that replicate the anatomical complexity, mechanical behaviour, and biological microenvironment of native organs.MethodsHere, we present a scalable, automated weaving strategy combining PLA multifilament cores with electrospun PCL nanofibre sheaths to fabricate biomimetic core-sheath yarns. These yarns were woven into tubular scaffolds with tunable architectures, enabling precise control over surface topography, porosity, and mechanical compliance.
